name: Gamaliel
overview: Gamaliel was a male leader of the tribe of Manasseh during the time of the Exodus. He held the position of head of the tribe during the census recorded in Numbers 1:10. His leadership role highlights his importance within the tribal structure of Israel during this formative period.
namesAndTitles: The name Gamaliel means 'recompense of G-d [El],' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew name. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaning that acknowledges divine recompense or reward.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Gamaliel was the father of Pedahzur, as explicitly stated in Numbers 1:10. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family connections are noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Gamaliel's significance lies in his leadership of the tribe of Manasseh during the Exodus, a critical moment in Israel's history. As head of his tribe at the time of the census, he represented his people in the organization and mobilization of Israel under God's direction. His role underscores the orderly and divinely appointed structure God established among the tribes.
